items.title: The divisor of a product of meromorphic sections is the sum of the divisors
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file divisors.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma says that for a locally Noetherian integral scheme the divisor of a product of nonzero meromorphic sections of two invertible modules is the sum of the two divisors, and hence that Weil divisor classes are additive in the tensor product (statement lines 6830-6845). The counted proof is short and complete: it fixes a prime divisor with generic point, chooses local generators of the two modules, observes that their product generates the tensor product, and factors the quotient of the product of the sections by the product of the generators into the product of the individual quotients, at which point additivity of the order function gives the claim (proof lines 6847-6863). It is H2: the computation is carried out in the counted span and the only input is additivity of the order of a meromorphic function.
